text:
alex: noticing weird tail latency pattern starting ~12:07 UTC after the canary push, saw sawtooth spikes every ~20s across a subset of GPUs
maria: saw it on the dashboard too, per-route p95 jumps from 90ms -> 600ms then back down, repeat
leo: any noisy tenant or OOMs? infra-bot: deploy-canary-2311 finished; no host OOMs reported
jen: dumping recent kernel-selector logs now, looks like we flip between kernel_v2_fused and kernel_legacy depending on microbatch parity
alex: parity? meaning odd vs even microbatch sizes? that's... unexpected
maria: exact: when admission groups end up with odd total microbatch (e.g., 3 vs 4) the kernel heuristic picks a different tiling/kern, profiler shows different launch config
leo: attached partial logs: 
```
[12:07:02] admission: group_id=723 size=3 max_seq=128 route=chat-davinci
[12:07:02] kernel_selector: chosen=kernel_v2_fused conf=tile=8x64 fallback_cost=1.3
[12:07:02] kv_cache: hits=0.78 miss=0.22
[12:07:22] admission: group_id=724 size=4 max_seq=128 route=chat-davinci
[12:07:22] kernel_selector: chosen=kernel_legacy conf=tile=16x32 fallback_cost=1.02
[12:07:22] kv_cache: hits=0.48 miss=0.52
```
maria: KV hit-rate drop lines up with kernel changes — suspect different memory layout / prefetch pattern causes KV eviction thrash for certain kernel layout
alex: ran a short perf profile on the hot GPU while reproducing. pprof flamegraph link: https://perf.internal/pprof/231111/odd-even.svg (private)
jen: quick snapshot from nvprof: 
```
GPU 0: kernel_v2_fused (sm_eff=0.78, occupancy=0.56, shared_mem=48KB) -> latency 12ms
GPU 0: kernel_legacy (sm_eff=0.92, occupancy=0.33, shared_mem=24KB) -> latency 95ms (but causes KV eviction storms)
```
leo: so kernel_legacy gives worse end-to-end due to KV thrashing even though per-kernel SM looks better. weird interplay between kernel memory access patterns and KV cache eviction thresholds
maria: hypothesis: kernel_legacy's smaller shared memory usage increases global memory traffic and causes KV cache lines to be pushed out due to memory pressure in our prefetcher, leading to higher tail latency
alex: can we force consistent kernel selection as a quick mitigation? maybe sticky kernel per-route/version or bias selector by penalizing kernels that increase global mem traffic metric
jen: tried a hot-patch: set KERNEL_SELECTOR_FORCE=fused for route chat-davinci on canary, tail latency stabilised in the next two cycles (p95 back to ~110ms). KV hit-rate returned to normal
leo: good sign. need longer soak though. also we should tweak admission to avoid odd/even resonance: pad microbatches to even sizes when route uses fused kernel ideally
maria: opened a perf issue with steps to repro + dataset + flamegraphs: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/INF-8731
alex: action items: 1) rollback selector roll that introduced heuristic change (jen) 2) add short-term sticky kernel override for affected routes (jen) 3) add admission padding experiment to smooth parity oscillation (leo) 4) follow-up deeper perf study on memory access patterns + KV prefetcher tuning (maria)
jen: I'm on (1) and (2) now, will post deploy id. infra-bot: rollback started for canary 2311 by jen at 12:14 UTC
alex: also update docs for kernel selector assumptions. this parity/resonance is subtle, add note to eng-runtime playbook
leo: logging improvement: record group_total_microbatch_parity in kernel_selector logs and kv_cache eviction_count per-cycle so we can correlate without full profiles
maria: thanks all. we'll keep the canary paused until soak completes. i'll run a synthetic workload to exercise odd/even boundaries overnight and report in morning
jen: rollback done, canary stable for 6m so far. 
alex: :thumbsup: nice catch everyone, this one would have been nasty in prod without quick kernel pin
infra-bot: incident: perf-regression-231111 created, severity=low, assignee=eng-runtime
jen: adding owner notes to the Jira and will link the hotpatch PR shortly
alex: cool. if anyone runs repro locally DM me the script and I'll attach my traces
